findings.ref: tests/resolve-project-context-block-check.py::main()/run_t003_case; reports/implementation/epic-193-a5-capability-resolver/T-003.md '## Outputs' and '### Outputs (this pass's own updates)'
findings.note: Four of the eleven T-003 fixtures main() executes -- resolve-component-paths-launch-failed, registry-discovery-unimportable, evaluate-predicate-output-malformed, dsl-warn-unsorted-affected-components -- have no content anywhere in this bundle and appear in NEITHER Outputs table, so their assertions cannot be credited. This is not merely a bundler gap: the report's own derivation method ('Derived from git status --short against this task's own uncommitted working tree') structurally cannot list files this task already committed in 82f6dbf2, so T-003's output declaration is itself incomplete and the bundler faithfully shipped what was declared. The consequence is load-bearing: dsl-warn-unsorted-affected-components is the ONLY assertion locking REQ-005/AC-024's ascending-lexicographic per-component fan-out (`sorted(affected_components)` in _evaluate_capabilities), and its entire discriminating power rests on its unshipped resolve-component-paths.py stub genuinely returning affected_components in DESCENDING order; a stub returning them already sorted would leave the expectation ['comp-a','comp-z'] passing against an unsorted implementation. The same applies to evaluate-predicate-output-malformed (sole coverage of step 7's dependency-output-malformed branch) and registry-discovery-unimportable. Contrast validate-capability-registry-launch-failed, which IS verifiable: its two files are declared with hashes a6b763fd.../87516d04..., byte-matching in-bundle fixture content, and its trigger is visible in the driver.

findings.ref: resolve-project-context.py::main() steps 7-8 except clauses; _evaluate_capabilities docstring; requirements.md REQ-004 diagnostics[] definition
findings.note: Already-collected severity: 'warn' diagnostics are silently discarded on every steps-7/8 abort. _evaluate_capabilities' docstring justifies its in-place mutation contract precisely as 'so a caller can still read every already-completed entry if a dependency subprocess failure aborts this function partway through', and states warn_diagnostics is 'likewise mutated in place'. But main()'s three handlers for that abort (except RegistryValidationFailed / DependencySubprocessFailed / DependencyOutputMalformed) pass capability_evaluations and OMIT warn_diagnostics, so every outcome: 'warn' node observed before the failing subprocess vanishes from the written Resolver Evidence. requirements.md REQ-004 defines diagnostics[] as 'recording every diagnostic-worthy condition this invocation encountered, not only the first/fatal one', and permits multiple block entries ('the one condition that itself caused, or jointly caused, this invocation's own fail-closed exit'). The code implements first/fatal-only, contradicting both the requirement and its own stated rationale. No fixture covers a WARN-then-dependency-failure invocation, so nothing can catch it.

REQ-004 specifies each severity: 'warn' entry's detail names that node's 'capability_id/component_id/(declaration_index, only for a conditional_facets[].when node)' location. _warn_diagnostic_detail unconditionally emits declaration_index, rendering `declaration_index=None` for every trigger-evaluation node. Uniqueness is preserved, so this is cosmetic drift, but the emitted string is not the shape the frozen requirement describes and the T-003 fixtures pin the drifted form.

Both files are the same size (13804 bytes per the assembler's elision notices), both begin at 'PASS: disabled-legacy-invocation: exit 1' with no header line, and their visible first/last 40 lines are byte-identical. The same table explains green-ps1 == green-sh by 'this driver's own output carries no runtime marker'; the two explanations are mutually exclusive. The likely real cause (per-run temp-directory names inside the elided FAIL detail lines) is benign, but the recorded provenance narrative is wrong in a task whose two prior Criticals were both about evidence-log fidelity.

Step 6 distinguishes canonicalizer-invocation-failed from dependency-subprocess-failed by testing for the substring 'canonicalizer-failed' in the dependency's stderr. generate-registry-digest.py is not in the bundle, so the stability of that token is unverifiable, and no fixture exercises the canonicalizer sub-branch (the dependency-subprocess-failed fixture's stub deliberately omits the token). A token change silently remaps a canonicalizer Block to the generic catch-all.
